title: SQLite schema decomposition
description: Objective: split SQLite schema management by manifest, migration, integrity, and bootstrap responsibility. Deliverable: focused internal schema modules preserving exact database behavior. NOT in scope: a schema version change or new table. Hard dependencies: none. Owned paths: packages/store/src/sqlite-schema.ts, new sqlite-schema-*.ts, and schema/bootstrap tests. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test.
definitionOfDone: Schema manifest, migration ordering, integrity checks, and bootstrap ambiguity outcomes are unchanged.
No database version, table, index, pragma, or stable error changes.
Every resulting production module is under 350 lines.
The focused store typecheck and test command exits 0.
taskRails: Refactor-only tasks preserve public contracts and stable errors.
Do not weaken or rewrite tests to make the split pass.
Stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

implementationPlan.description: Before extraction, treat the existing schema suites as immutable characterization: map each current assertion to identity/fresh-database refusal, exact manifest/DDL tamper detection, v1 empty migration and populated refusal, project binding/scope evidence, semantic ledger and sqlite_sequence integrity, too-new/no-mutation behavior, bootstrap COMMIT/rollback ambiguity, busy normalization, and Node strip-types entrypoint loading. Do not edit, skip, reorder, or weaken these tests; no new test is needed because this task changes no behavior and the focused hostile coverage already exercises every moved branch.

Characterization mapped, nothing edited. No test added, per plan — this is a behavior-neutral extraction and the existing hostile suites are the oracle.

Move seams confirmed against the real file — `sqlite-schema.ts` is 648 lines with exactly the 5 exports the plan names (canonicalDatabasePath, isFreshDatabaseFileCandidate, compareVersions, isSqliteBusy, bootstrapAndValidateSchema). Line map: imports 1-31; canonicalDatabasePath 33-57; isFreshDatabaseFileCandidate 58-72; isFreshDatabase 73-114; normalizeSchemaSql 115-118; validateExactSchemaObjects 119-163; validateSchemaManifestMetadata 164-182; validateSchema 183-379; resolveProjectBinding 380-485; compareVersions 486-503; migrateLocked 504-583; isSqliteBusy 584-595; bootstrapAndValidateSchema 596-648.

Projected module sizes, all inside the 250-line rail: conformance ~68 (115-182), integrity ~197 (183-379), migration ~80 (504-583), bootstrap ~212 (73-114 + 380-485 + 584-648), residual facade ~110. Integrity and bootstrap are the tight ones — if imports push either past 250 I will report rather than silently split differently.

THE LOAD-BEARING RISK, quantified: the suites assert error CODES, not messages or check order. Code histogram across all store tests — STORE_CORRUPT 34, STORE_INPUT_INVALID 12, STORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED 10, STORE_UNAVAILABLE 4, STORE_SCHEMA_INVALID 4, STORE_BUSY 2, STORE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED 1, STORE_CLOSED 1. So a green suite does NOT prove the move was faithful: reordering two checks that both raise STORE_CORRUPT, or altering a message string, passes 112/112 silently. STORE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED with a single assertion means the populated/advanced-sequence refusal path in migrateLocked is the thinnest-covered branch I will touch. Per `gotcha-verbatim-move-refactor-proof` I will prove each move by mechanical body-diff against HEAD in step 6, not by reading, and will not treat the green gate as sufficient evidence.

Shim convention verified live: every non-test `.ts` in `packages/store/src` has a tracked sibling `.js` containing exactly `export * from "./<name>.ts";`. Only exceptions are `index.js` (package export resolves `./src/index.ts` directly) and the two `*-test-helpers.js`. The 4 new modules therefore need 4 shims in the same commit — omitting one fails neither tsc nor Vitest, only `store-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts` with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.

VERBATIM PROOF: all four moved bodies diffed together against HEAD ranges 73-114, 380-485, 584-648 (isFreshDatabase, resolveProjectBinding, isSqliteBusy, bootstrapAndValidateSchema), blank-normalized — IDENTICAL, 203 lines, zero drift. Original relative order kept, so the file reads in the same sequence as HEAD.

Preserved verbatim in the ambiguity path, which is the subtlest logic in the task: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` with its STORE_BUSY-vs-STORE_UNAVAILABLE split on the startup lock ("database startup lock timed out" / "unable to acquire database startup lock"); the `commitAttempted` flag set immediately BEFORE `database.exec("COMMIT")`; `transactionEndedAfterCommitAttempt = commitAttempted && !database.isTransaction`; conditional ROLLBACK guarded by `database.isTransaction` with its own try/catch; the `causes` array built as `[error]` or `[error, rollbackError]`; OUTCOME_UNKNOWN taking precedence over the STORE_BUSY check that follows it; and the distinct bootstrap-phase "database bootstrap timed out" message. The two STORE_BUSY messages differ only by phase and are trivially swappable by hand — confirmed unswapped by the diff. Order migrate -> validateSchema -> resolveProjectBinding -> COMMIT unchanged.
